threat_event: Adversary-in-the-middle phishing steals a session from the Controller or Senior Accountant; the attacker takes over the mailbox, hides replies with inbox rules, and redirects a family or subsidiary payment
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Push MFA without number matching and no phishing-resistant MFA; no alerts on new inbox rules or forwarding; email is the channel for payment requests and approvals
regulatory_driver: 16 CFR 314.4(c)(5); 16 CFR 314.4(c)(8); CSF 2.0 profile PR.AA-03 (voluntary benchmark)
existing_controls: MFA push on SYS-02; bank dual approval; yearly awareness video
treatment_plan: Phishing-resistant security keys for the 7 staff and for every administrator; sign-in limited to managed devices; alerts for new inbox rules, forwarding, and sign-ins from new countries, routed to the MSP and the Family Office Director; payment-fraud training with simulations

threat_event: A spoofed or look-alike email that appears to come from a family member, subsidiary, or vendor gets staff to change payee bank details or send a wire to a fraudster's account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Callback habit is unwritten and unrecorded; payee bank-detail changes accepted by email; a $48,000 attempt in March 2026 was caught only because the amount was unusual
existing_controls: Bank dual approval; staff experience
treatment_plan: Written payment verification procedure: callback to a number already on file for every new payee, bank-detail change, and wire over $10,000, recorded in the payment log; second staff member confirms; quarterly review of the log by the Family Office Director

threat_event: Theft of family members' records (tax returns with SSNs, passports, estate plans, travel schedules) from the Family site after an account compromise leads to identity theft, extortion, or physical risk to family members
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: All 7 staff can open every family folder; 17 years of tax returns and ID copies kept; no data inventory
existing_controls: MFA on SYS-02; vault folders per family member
treatment_plan: Per-family-member folders with need-to-know groups; move IDs and tax returns out of the Family site into the vault; data inventory; disposal of records past the retention schedule (R-012)

threat_event: Staff see family documents they do not need, and the AI assistant surfaces them in summaries, leading to accidental disclosure inside or outside the office
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Family site open to all staff; AI assistant reaches everything a user can reach; a trust distribution memo surfaced to the Executive Assistant on 2026-07-22
existing_controls: None beyond trust in staff
treatment_plan: Restructure Family site permissions before the AI pilot resumes; sensitivity labels on estate, tax, and medical folders that the assistant cannot read; quarterly access review

threat_event: An attacker who obtains the MSP's shared global administrator credentials, or compromises the MSP's tools, takes full control of the tenant, reads all mail and files, and deletes data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared MSP admin account with MFA on the help desk phone; no record of which technicians use it; MSP contract has no security terms
regulatory_driver: 16 CFR 314.4(f)(2); 16 CFR 314.4(c)(5); CSF 2.0 profile GV.SC-05 (voluntary benchmark)
existing_controls: MSP is a long-standing provider; admin actions appear in the suite audit log
treatment_plan: Replace the shared account with named MSP admin accounts protected by security keys; just-in-time admin rights; contract amendment with security terms, 24-hour incident notice, and a technician list; annual MSP security review

threat_event: Email and files in the productivity suite are deleted or encrypted (by an attacker or by mistake) and cannot be recovered beyond the vendor's retention window
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No independent backup of SYS-02; synced folders on laptops would carry encrypted files to the cloud
existing_controls: Vendor deleted-item retention
treatment_plan: Independent SaaS backup of mail and files with one-year retention in a separate account the MSP's daily admin cannot delete; quarterly restore test

threat_event: SYS-11 is compromised through its exposed remote desktop port or an unpatched operating system; snapshots in the same account are deleted; K-1 data is lost and partners' SSNs are exposed
threat_source: Cybercriminal scanning for exposed remote desktop
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Remote desktop open to the internet with an IP allowlist only; operating system reaches end of support in October 2026; snapshots in the same account; no restore test
regulatory_driver: 16 CFR 314.4(c)(3); 16 CFR 314.4(d)(1); CSF 2.0 profile PR.PS-02 (voluntary benchmark)
existing_controls: IP allowlist; monthly MSP patching; daily snapshots
treatment_plan: Close the remote desktop port and reach SYS-11 only through the MSP's MFA-protected gateway; upgrade the operating system before end of support; copy snapshots to a separate account; restore test; decide by 2027-03-31 whether to move to a SaaS partnership accounting service

threat_event: A former employee or subsidiary guest keeps access and reads board packs or family files
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Guest accounts never reviewed; no offboarding checklist; a former Marine Supply controller kept access for 6 months
existing_controls: Office Manager removes staff accounts when told
treatment_plan: Offboarding checklist for staff and guests; subsidiaries must report guest departures within 1 business day (management agreement); guest accounts expire every 180 days unless renewed; monthly reconciliation

threat_event: A family member's vault account is taken over through SIM swapping or a shared password, exposing that family's estate, tax, and identity documents
threat_source: Cybercriminal; account sharing within the family
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Two family members use SMS codes; the Principal's spouse used the Principal's account until 2026-08-20
existing_controls: Vault MFA (SMS or app)
treatment_plan: Authenticator app or security key for every family user; separate account for each family member (spouse's account created 2026-08-20); short family security briefing

threat_event: The MSP cannot restore laptops, the network, or SYS-11 in time, or handles family data without adequate safeguards, because the contract sets no recovery time or security requirements
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP contract has a 4-business-hour response time only, no recovery commitment, no security terms, and no subcontractor list
existing_controls: Long relationship; MSP responsive in practice
treatment_plan: Contract amendment at renewal: recovery times that meet the BIA, security schedule, incident notice within 24 hours, subcontractor list, right to evidence; annual review

threat_event: A SaaS vendor that holds family data (investment platform, bill pay, payroll, vault) is breached and family information is exposed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No list of service providers with access to family data; SOC 2 reports received but never reviewed; contracts not checked for safeguards
existing_controls: Vendors are established providers; SOC 2 reports on file for two
treatment_plan: Service provider list with data held and contract terms; annual SOC 2 or questionnaire review, starting with the investment platform (P09); security terms at renewal

threat_event: A breach exposes records that should no longer be kept (tax returns since 2009, former household employees' forms), raising the harm and the number of people to notify
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No retention schedule or disposal procedure
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Retention schedule approved by counsel and the CPA firm; disposal of family and employee records past it, with a disposal log; yearly review

threat_event: Staff or family members paste family statements or documents into free public AI chatbots, which keep and may use the data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No approved-tools list before 2026-09; an adult grandchild pasted a custodian statement into a public chatbot in July 2026
existing_controls: None
treatment_plan: Approved-tools rule in POL-02 Part C; family security briefing; web filter blocks free chatbots on office devices

threat_event: A staff laptop or personal phone with email and MFA is lost or stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops encrypted; personal phones unmanaged, with email apps and MFA authenticators
existing_controls: Laptop disk encryption
treatment_plan: App protection policy for email and files on personal phones (PIN, no local save, remote wipe of company data); report losses within 1 hour

threat_event: The cyber insurer denies or reduces a social engineering fraud claim because callbacks were not documented as the policy requires
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Policy requires documented verification of payment changes; no payment log exists
existing_controls: Policy in force
treatment_plan: Payment log (R-002) kept in the form the insurer requires; confirm the requirement with the broker at renewal

threat_event: Slow, disorganized response to an incident delays containment and misses notice deadlines (Florida 30 days)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident response plan; only one person knows the insurer hotline; near misses are not logged
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(4); CSF 2.0 profile RS.MA-01 (voluntary benchmark)
existing_controls: Insurance with breach hotline
treatment_plan: POL-03 and the P08 runbook; printed contact card; incident log; first tabletop with the MSP

threat_event: The office loses the Advisers Act family office exclusion because a staff member holds the office out as an adviser or advice reaches a non-family person
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written check of who may receive advice; a staff professional profile described the office as offering investment advisory services until 2026-08-13
existing_controls: Counsel reviews the exclusion every two years
treatment_plan: Written rule on family-client eligibility and communications in POL-02 Part A; yearly confirmation by the Investment Director; counsel review before any new client or co-investment

threat_event: A compromised subsidiary account or mailbox is used to phish the office or upload malicious files to the Subsidiaries site
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Subsidiaries run their own IT with varying controls; 9 guest accounts; trusted sender relationship
existing_controls: Antivirus on office laptops; MFA required for guests
treatment_plan: Minimum security terms in the management agreements (MFA, incident notice to the office within 24 hours); yearly one-page attestation from each subsidiary President; guest access limited to its own folder

threat_event: The office internet line fails for a day
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One line, no failover
existing_controls: All systems are SaaS; staff can work from home on managed laptops
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Family Office Director: working from home covers an outage at no cost

threat_event: A hurricane closes the office for several days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Florida location
existing_controls: SaaS systems; laptops go home before a storm
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Family Office Director with a one-page storm checklist (laptops and tokens home, contact card, bank approver backup)

threat_event: The multifunction printer or conference-room PC is exploited through outdated firmware or software
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Printer firmware not on the MSP patch schedule; conference PC shared login
existing_controls: Firewall blocks inbound traffic
treatment_plan: MSP updated printer firmware and added it to monthly patching; conference PC given a kiosk account with no file access (both done 2026-08-21)

threat_event: A bank token is lost or an approver is unavailable, so payments cannot be released on time
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One token per approver; Principal is backup approver but rarely uses the portal
existing_controls: Banks can issue replacement tokens in 1 to 2 business days
treatment_plan: Principal practices a test approval each quarter; tokens stored in the office safe overnight

threat_event: One staff member changes a payee's bank details in the bill pay platform and pays the new account with no second approval
threat_source: Cybercriminal using a compromised account; insider
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Bill pay platform roles allow the Senior Accountant to edit payees and release payments alone (found in P07 testing 2026-09-01)
existing_controls: Payments come from family accounts with bank fraud monitoring
treatment_plan: Turn on the platform's dual approval for payee changes and payments over $5,000; Controller approves; weekly payee change report
